Reviewer: wopr pool job review-4416, claude-opus-5-5, mkinney (.claude-bob); did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review, because the PR changes posted G-code (closed 2D Chamfer passes now post G2/G3).

Reviewer record: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/4416#issuecomment-7226216199

## What looks good

- `chamfer_with_tolerance` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/chamfer.rs:158`) uses the existing sided fitter (`fit_arcs_sided`). The fit tolerance is the lower of the operation tolerance and `ARC_FIT_TOL` (0.01 mm). A tolerance that is zero, negative or NaN falls back to `ARC_FIT_TOL` in `fit_arcs_sided` (`arcs.rs:147`). No new panic path.
- The air side is correct. I examined the four cases by hand against `arc_side::sided` (`part_in = air_left != ccw`), with `air_left = climb`:
  - boss, climb: CW arc, part on the centre side.
  - boss, conventional: CCW arc, part on the centre side.
  - bore, climb: CCW arc, part off the centre side.
  - bore, conventional: CW arc, part off the centre side.
  This agrees with the comment at `chamfer.rs:176` ("material right of travel" under climb).
- `run_level_walks` with `Some(&walks)` is the same ladder that `run_levels(.., None, ..)` used, with fitted walks. Endpoints, depth, feed and direction stay. The motion pin asserts all of these for boss and bore, climb and conventional, and zero and 0.6 mm cone setback.
- `path.breaks` still comes from the original loops, not from the moves. Thus the edge-break gate judges the fitted ride against the authored promise.
- The open model-edge path does not change.
- The app pin posts through the normal Haas post and the stock gate.
- No recorded program moved. `example_catalog` posts each committed `.nc` byte for byte, and the `2d/edge-work` case (which has a 2D Chamfer) stays the same.
- The body has `Changelog:` and ends with `Fixes #4411`. There is a decision file. No UI change, no process file, no new dependency.

## Results (locally, trial merge with upstream/main 878f8c2f2627387a59f3b94c0e18aa84a8fdd280, clean)

The quick plan maps the diff to 323 steps (`generate.rs` maps to all app suites). I ran the chamfer, stamp, edge-break, golden and catalog suites. All passed:

- `camcraft-motion` lib: 768 passed, 22 ignored.
- motion `chamfer_circular` 11/11, `chamfer_minimum_radius` 9/9, `chamfer_open_refusals` 3/3.
- `camcraft-app` lib: 329 passed.
- app `chamfer_minimum_radius` 3, `chamfer_modelled_edge` 8, `chamfer_open_edges` 6, `chamfer_partly_bevelled` 2, `mcp_chamfer_minimum_radius` 1, `setup_align_chamfer` 2, `stock_chamfer_added_part` 3, `deburr_cache_stamp` 5, `stock_stamp` 4, `stale_rapid_law` 2, `wire_stamp` 8, `edge_break_bound` 5, `edge_break_gate` 5.
- Goldens and catalog: `example_catalog` 44 passed, 4 ignored (heavy lane). `example_catalog_edge_work` 1, `first_part_programs` 2, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `golden_cl` 34.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Extra suites run: none owed. The diff does not touch `testdata/` or the import code.

Heavy lanes: not run. No heavy record names this head. The diff does not reach a heavy-lane case that the light catalog run does not cover.

## Mutations

1. Walk the passes without the fitted walks (`run_level_walks(.., None, ..)`): RED. `closed_model_chamfer_preserves_circular_interpolation` and `closed_model_chamfer_posts_haas_arcs_through_the_stock_gate` fail.
2. Flip the air side (`Some(!p.climb)`): GREEN. No suite fails. See note 1.
3. Remove the stamp salt `closed-model-chamfer-arcs-4411`: GREEN. No suite fails. See note 2.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Optional, non-blocking (follow-ups, P7)

1. No test pins the air side of the fit. The pin uses an exact sampled circle, and on such a circle each vertex is in the slack of `sided`, so the side has no effect. A pin with one vertex pushed off the circle toward the part (boss and bore) would catch a wrong side. The current code is correct. The stock gate also holds a gouge over 0.01 mm. Thus this is a missing test, not wrong output.
2. No test pins the stale-once stamp salt (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs:88`). Without the salt, an old linear cache stays valid. That cache was verified when it was made, so this is not a safety issue.
3. `docs/decisions/4411-model-chamfer-arcs.md` does not use the format of `docs/decisions/README.md`. Use a `## #4411 - <title>` heading, and add what was dropped and the cost to change later.
4. `chamfer.rs` is now 437 lines (423 before). It was already over the 400-line limit.
5. Question for the maintainer: the commit type is `perf`, but the change makes posted G-code different (arcs in place of lines) and the issue has `enhancement`. If this is a `feat`, it merges at the next cut, not when reviewed.

Not exercised: a real controller run, and the heavy lanes.
